steps.message:
# Reconcile the reservations of kit orders

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server. Free stock is in the warehouse `main`, and units held for open sales orders are in the warehouse `reserved`.

The component reservations of several kit and bundle orders no longer match the orders. Reconcile them. Everything you need is in `/app/kits/`:

- `policy.md`: how reservations, releases and picks are posted, how kits explode into components, which revision of a kit applies, how order lines are amended, and which substitutions are allowed. Follow it.
- `open-orders.csv`: the orders to reconcile, one row per amendment of an order line: order id, line, amendment number, the date the order was created, the sku ordered (a kit or a stocked sku), the quantity and the status.
- `kit-bom.csv`: the components of each kit by revision, with the date each revision took effect.

What to do:

1. For every order in `open-orders.csv`, make the reservation the order holds for each sku equal to what the policy says it should hold. Use `adjust_stock` with the order id as reference, as the policy describes. Some reservations are right, and some are not.
2. Write `/app/kit-reservations.csv`, a CSV file with the header `order,sku,required,picked,reserved` and one row for each order in `open-orders.csv` and each sku that the order requires or that has a posting in `reserved` under the order, including rows that need no change. All three quantities are in each: `required` is the units of the sku the order requires, `picked` the units picked under the order that count toward the sku, and `reserved` the reservation the order holds for the sku when you are done.

Do not change anything for orders that are not in `open-orders.csv`, and do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

arguments.command: cd /app/kits; cat policy.md; cat open-orders.csv; cat kit-bom.csv

results.content:
# Kit orders: reservations, picks and reconciliation

## Warehouses and postings

Free stock is kept in the warehouse `main`. Units held for an open sales order are kept in the
warehouse `reserved`. Every posting below is an `adjust_stock` call with the order id (`SO-...`) as
reference. All quantities are in each, the stock unit of every component.

- Reservation: the quantity out of `main` and the same quantity into `reserved`, both with reason
  `transfer`.
- Release: the quantity out of `reserved` and the same quantity into `main`, both with reason
  `transfer`.
- Pick: one adjustment with reason `shipment` and a negative delta. Pickers take reserved units out
  of `reserved`. A unit taken from the shelf instead, and every substitute, is posted out of `main`.
  Both count as picked for the order.

The reservation an order holds for a sku is the net of all postings in `reserved` with that sku and
the order's reference: reservations, minus releases, minus picks out of `reserved`.

## Kits

Kits and bundles are not stocked. `kit-bom.csv` lists the components of each kit by revision. A
component of a kit can itself be a kit: explode it as well, multiplying the quantities down the
tree, until only stocked skus remain. A sku that is not a kit in `kit-bom.csv` is stocked, and an
order line for it reserves the sku itself.

A revision applies from its `effective_from` date, that day included, until the next revision of
the same kit takes effect. Every kit in an order's tree, nested kits included, uses the revision in
effect on the date the order was created, whatever revision is in effect today.

## Order lines

`open-orders.csv` has one row per amendment of an order line. Amendment 0 is the line as it was
entered. The row with the highest amendment number of a line is in effect and replaces the earlier
rows of that line. A line whose row in effect has status `cancelled` requires nothing.

## Substitutions

A picker may ship a substitute in place of a component only where this table allows it, for the kit
whose bill of materials lists the component. `ratio` units of the substitute replace one unit of
the component.

| kit | component | substitute | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| KT-10 | CP-202 | CP-213 | 1 |
| KT-10 | CP-203 | CP-214 | 2 |
| KT-20 | CP-204 | CP-218 | 1 |

A substitute pick counts toward the component when the order's tree holds a kit that allows that
substitution. Otherwise it counts toward nothing, and the component it replaced is still required.
Substitutes are never reserved.

## Reconciliation

For each order and each sku:

1. Required: the units of the sku that the order's lines in effect require, after exploding kits.
2. Picked: the units of the sku picked under the order, plus the substitute picks that count toward
   it, divided by their ratio.
3. The order should hold the required units minus the picked units in `reserved`, and nothing when
   more was picked than is required. Reserve what is missing. Release the excess, including the
   whole reservation of a sku the order no longer requires.

steps.reasoning_content: I have 338 adjustments to sort through, and I only need the ones tied to SO-55xx references. That's 17 orders, so querying each reference separately would mean a lot of paged calls at 5 per page. Filtering by the reserved warehouse might not be enough, since some picks come from main, so I'm considering filtering by reference for each order instead.
I'll page through everything in parallel, since the totals show several pages per SKU. Not sure there's a local database to query, so paging through the API is the way to go.
I'm picking up the page range from 5504, pages 2 through 6, along with lines 5507 through 5512.

I'm going through the 5504 page 1 results, noting that adj-47 CP-217 has 4 reserved. I still need to cover the rest of the pages: 5507 pages 2 through 4, 5508 page 2, 5509 pages 2 through 5, 5510 pages 2 through 5, 5511 pages 2 and 3, and 5512 page 2.

Checking the order 5508 against its two items, then I'm tallying the bill-of-materials lines for KT-10 and KT-20 across the before and after September cutoff.

Checking the KT-20 and KT-40 bills of materials against the order lines, then working through order 5501's reservations and picks to find which release is needed.

Now I'm working out what the 5503 order should reserve for KT-30, since its KT-10 components were never posted and the 216 stock was picked from the shelf. Then I'll move on to order 5504 for KT-40 and check which bill of materials applies.

I'm working out the totals for the KT-40 order: its KT-30 and KT-20 sub-assemblies roll up into the same shared parts as the KT-10 lines, so I'm adding those counts up per part number and comparing them against what's already posted.

I'm checking the 204 count for KT-20: the two substitute picks from the main stock cover the KT-20 need, so 204 should be held at 2 and its extra reservation released. Then I'm raising the KT-20 reservation for 207 to 4, since only 2 are posted so far.

I'm reconciling order 5505, where the KT-20 line needs 207 at 4 and 208 at 2, and the posted counts for 207, 208 and 204 run higher, so I'm releasing the extras. Then order 5506 gets cut back to just the 207 reservation, since its line 1 was cancelled and everything else posted for it should come off. I'm now starting on order 5507, a KT-10 order dated 08-30 that falls under the earlier bill of materials.

Now I'm checking the 5507 order against the earlier bill of materials: the six KT-10 lines each need one, the 204 line has its reservation released and has to be re-reserved, and the 218 substitution doesn't count toward anything.

I'm releasing the surplus on order 5508: 207 drops by 3, and 208 and 204 each drop by 2 so they match what the order needs. Then I'm moving to order 5509, a KT-10 order under the later bill of materials, and checking its reservations and picks line by line.

I'm releasing one unit of 203 on order 5509, since its pick from the substitute covers part of the need. Then I'm moving on to order 5510, a KT-30 order under the later bill of materials, and checking its reservations against the posted counts line by line.

I'm checking the 5511 reservations against the posted counts, and they match once the picks are netted out. Next up is order 5512, which is dated 09-12, so it falls under the later bill of materials and I need to recheck its KT-20 line.

Now I'm going through the adjustments: I'll mark the extra reservations for 210 and release the surplus entries across orders 5501 through 5512.

I'm going to reserve the missing quantities first, drawing from main stock, and only then move the releases back to main, since reservations that fail for lack of stock would otherwise be left half-done.

steps.message:
I reconciled the reservations for all twelve orders, SO-5501 to SO-5512, wrote `/app/kit-reservations.csv`, and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

I did not re-query the inventory service after the adjustments to confirm the final reserved quantities. The CSV is computed from the policy and the existing postings. Each adjustment call returned the expected new on-hand figure.

SO-5510 and SO-5511 already matched the policy, so I changed nothing for them.

What I changed on the others:
- **SO-5501:** released 1 CP-202. The CP-213 pick is a valid substitute for it, so one unit counts as picked.
- **SO-5502:** released CP-211 (revision A component) and reserved CP-206 and CP-212 (revision B).
- **SO-5503:** the order date makes KT-10 revision B apply, so I reserved all seven KT-10 components ×2. I also released 2 CP-216, which a shelf pick had already covered.
- **SO-5504:** released 1 CP-204 (the CP-218 substitute counts for it), and reserved 2 CP-207 and 1 CP-208 that were short.
- **SO-5505:** trimmed the reservation to the amended quantity of 2 KT-20, releasing 1 CP-208, 2 CP-207 and 1 CP-204.
- **SO-5506:** released everything for the cancelled KT-10 line and kept the 2 CP-207 from the second line.
- **SO-5507:** reserved 1 CP-204. The CP-218 pick doesn't count because there is no KT-20 in this order's tree, so CP-204 is still required.
- **SO-5508:** released 3 CP-207, 2 CP-208 and 2 CP-204 after the amendment to 2 KT-20.
- **SO-5509:** released 1 CP-203, because the 2 CP-214 picked count as 1 CP-203.
- **SO-5512:** KT-20 revision B applies, so I reserved 1 CP-210.

I did not touch any orders outside `open-orders.csv`.
